The user now explicitly requests a NEW bounded experiment returning to the original HEXAGONAL CELL partition, not center-owned dots or disks. They want reasonably rounded cells rather than the elongated shapes produced earlier. Please use the actual retained 5,986 Manhattan pickup coordinates and the original 38-cell shared-vertex hexagonal partition, with full modeled Manhattan coverage, no gaps/overlaps, and convex six-sided underlying cells.

NEW CONSTRAINT: maximum directional width / minimum directional width <= 2 for EACH cell. Define this precisely as maximum Feret diameter (max vertex pair distance) divided by minimum caliper width (minimum projection span onto normals of polygon edges), computed on the actual geometry; do not substitute an axis-aligned bounding box ratio or averaged compactness score. Explicitly distinguish underlying six-sided cell geometry from its intersection with the Manhattan domain. For shape usefulness, report compactness on BOTH underlying cells and actual clipped service regions; if strict <=2 on clipped geography is impossible or initialization infeasible, explain with evidence instead of silently excluding clipped cells. Inspect historical geometry first; determine whether the initial 38-cell state is feasible under the constraint. Do not start from the highly elongated already-balanced state and claim it obeys the new bound.

Use the established local shared-corner / coordinated-neighbor movement and local imbalance-based annealing strategy from the successful hexagon experiment, but reject moves violating full coverage, no overlap, convexity or the 2:1 compactness bound. Keep all cells six-sided before clipping. Load SUCCESS is every actual cell within +/-10% of N/38 = 157.5263158 (integer counts 142..173). We seek whether both balance and shape are achievable. First build/verify a feasible initial geometry; if exact 38 cells plus domain makes that impossible, distinguish failure to construct from a proved impossibility, and report the concrete issue.

Execute a meaningful simulation on the full data, retaining reproducible data/code, initial/final geometry and per-cell counts/shape ratios. Give a clear result: did it meet both targets, how long, worst width ratio, load CV, min/max, and geographical RMS to actual assigned-group centroids. Compare against historical 38-region k-means+merging (CV .235290714, centroid RMS .446803116 km) and historical balanced hexagons (CV .003169674, centroid RMS .499703266 km), but label those unconstrained on the new ratio. Produce a before/after map if possible so the user can judge elongation, prioritizing truthful metrics. If a run is stopped for time or lack of progress, call it UNFINISHED / no feasible balanced result found, never equate a cap with convergence or mathematical infeasibility. Do not continue the abandoned all-movable vertex-owned rule-2 runs; they were stopped after collapse. Please perform the requested experiment and report promptly if a blocker prevents execution.

The obstruction is confirmed. Any 2:1 clipped region containing the northern tip can contain at most **89 pickups**, but balance requires at least **142**.

Before stopping, the constrained search completed over 420 rounds and reached CV **0.242439**, with loads **0–181**. The best saved geometry still passes both 2:1 bounds, full coverage, convexity, and no-overlap checks. I’m saving that geometry, the before/after map, and the impossibility certificate.

Udi, **I constructed a feasible compact 38-cell partition and ran constrained balancing on all 5,986 pickups. But the joint balance target and strict 2:1 bound on clipped service regions are mathematically incompatible with this modeled geography and dataset.**

The ratio used was exactly
\[
R(P)=\frac{\max_{a,b\in P}\|a-b\|}{\min_{\|n\|=1}\left(\max_{p\in P}n\cdot p-\min_{p\in P}n\cdot p\right)}.
\]
The minimum was evaluated at convex-hull edge normals. This also gives the directional widths of nonconvex clipped regions; actual intersections—not their hulls—determined ownership and coverage.

The original regular state was **infeasible**: clipped ratio 7.6715 and a 0.26558 km² coverage gap. Geometry repair found a feasible start in two rounds. The subsequent local shared-corner/coordinated-neighbor annealing rejected violations of coverage, convexity, and either width-ratio bound.

| State, all K=38 | CV | Min–max load | Centroid RMS km | Worst underlying ratio | Worst clipped ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Constructed feasible start | 1.611678 | 0–1,021 | .627083 | 1.934975 | 1.964748 |
| Best constrained iterate | .242439 | 0–181 | .443921 | 1.999776 | 1.999876 |
| Historical K-means + merging¹ | .235291 | 88–200 | .446803 | — | — |
| Historical balanced hexagons¹ | .003170 | 157–158 | .499703 | 11.732166 | 11.220937 |

¹ Historical solutions were unconstrained on the new ratio.

The best constrained iterate occurred at **round 412**. Over 420 rounds ran in approximately 35 seconds. Independent verification found convex six-sided underlying cells, zero overlap, complete modeled coverage within numerical tolerance, and exactly one assignment for every pickup.

**The obstruction is at the northern tip:**

- The entire modeled domain has minimum caliper width **4.273568 km**.
- Every clipped service region therefore has minimum width at most that value.
- A region with ratio ≤2 must consequently have diameter ≤**8.547137 km**.
- Within that distance of the domain vertex **(9.114, 19.469) km**, there are only **89 pickups**.
- Full coverage requires a region containing this vertex, but that region cannot reach the required **142 pickups**.

Thus **no partition can meet both requirements**, regardless of the optimizer. This proof concerns the **clipped-region** bound; it does not rule out balance with the bound imposed only on underlying hexagons.

I stopped after establishing the obstruction. The saved best iterate is **not a balanced solution**, and no simulation remains running.
